record.original_question: Which properties of the velocity field are sufficient to guarantee the existence of a unique global smooth solution of the three-dimensional incompressible Navier-Stokes equations for all times, assuming the initial conditions are already smooth? This asks for structural conditions on the evolving velocity field that rule out singularity formation and ensure global regularity.

evidence.quote: Question 3.3. Following the previous questions, which properties of the velocity field would be needed to guarantee the existence of a (unique) global smooth solution at all times, once the initial conditions are smooth?
Unfortunately, there is no way to prove that the L4(IR3) norm of the velocity field is bounded at all times based solely on Navier-Stokes equations.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the three-dimensional incompressible Navier-Stokes equations on $\mathbb{R}^3$ for an unknown velocity field $u(x,t):\mathbb{R}^3	imes[0,\infty)	o\mathbb{R}^3$ and pressure $p(x,t):\mathbb{R}^3	imes[0,\infty)	o\mathbb{R}$:

$$\partial_t u + (u\cdot\nabla) u = -\nabla p + \nu\,\Delta u, \qquad \nabla\cdot u = 0,$$

with viscosity $\nu>0$ and divergence-free initial data $u(\cdot,0)=u_0\in C^\infty(\mathbb{R}^3;\mathbb{R}^3)$ that decays sufficiently rapidly at infinity (for instance, Schwartz class).

Determine a structural property $\mathcal{P}$ of the evolving velocity field $u(\cdot,t)$ that is both sharp and verifiable, with the following meaning: if $\mathcal{P}$ holds along the evolution starting from any such smooth initial datum $u_0$, then there exists a unique solution $u\in C^\infty(\mathbb{R}^3\times[0,\infty))$ that remains smooth for all $t\ge 0$ (i.e., no finite-time singularity forms). Equivalently, identify a quantity or qualitative feature of $u$ — beyond the known classical regularity criteria such as $u\in L^s_t L^q_x$ with $\frac{2}{s}+\frac{3}{q}\le 1$, $q>3$ (Ladyzhenskaya–Prodi–Serrin), the Beale–Kato–Majda condition $\int_0^T \|\omega(\cdot,t)\|_{L^\infty}\,dt<\infty$ on the vorticity $\omega=\nabla\times u$, and Escauriaza–Seregin–Šverák's $u\in L^\infty_t L^3_x$ — whose validity along solutions can be derived from the Navier-Stokes system itself and that suffices to rule out blow-up, thereby yielding global smooth existence.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is a refined form of the global regularity problem for the 3D incompressible Navier-Stokes equations, one of the Clay Millennium Problems, and remains open. Numerous conditional regularity criteria are known (Ladyzhenskaya–Prodi–Serrin, Beale–Kato–Majda, Escauriaza–Seregin–Šverák $L^\infty_t L^3_x$, Constantin–Fefferman vorticity-direction criterion, etc.), but no property derivable a priori from the equations themselves is known to imply global smoothness.

status_evidence.title: Navier–Stokes existence and smoothness — Clay Millennium Problem
status_evidence.snippet: The Clay Mathematics Institute lists the global existence and smoothness of solutions to the 3D incompressible Navier-Stokes equations as an unsolved Millennium Prize Problem.
status_evidence.claim: Global regularity for 3D Navier-Stokes is an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Escauriaza, Seregin, Šverák, L^{3,∞}-solutions of the Navier-Stokes equations
status_evidence.snippet: Solutions bounded in $L^\infty_t L^3_x$ cannot develop singularities; one of the strongest known regularity criteria.
status_evidence.claim: Strong conditional regularity criteria are known but a property guaranteed by the equations themselves is not.
